newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma ranges, bonds well bid, depos hold.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma ranges, bonds well bid, depos hold.

text.p: Greek fixed-coupon bonds were firmer late on Monday after the successful launch of the government's first index-linked paper, traders said.
A monetary source told Reuters that Greece raised more than 120 billion drachmas from the sale of 4.0 percent, five and 10-year CPI-indexed bonds on Monday.

"There has been very little price movement and trade in depos and forex forwards today," said a dealer at a private bank. "Almost half of continental Europe is on holiday and this tends to depress volume locally."
Bonds dealers said fixed coupon bonds were well bid with prices rising quarter of a point, bond dealers said.

"Banks opted for fixed coupon paper rather than buy heavily into the CPI-indexed bonds," said a dealer. "Still, the ministry should be happy raising over 100 billion drachmas in its first try when its annual target is 300 billion drachmas."
Other dealers said there was little movement in FRN prices.
The mark was quoted at 159.44/49 from Friday's 159.495 fix, the dollar at 270.16/26 drachmas from 271.300 and the ecu at 311.12/22 from 311.440 drachmas.
"Ecu has firmed a bit against the drachma after the fixing, trading currently at 311.25/35," said a dealer at a private bank.
Other forex dealers said they expected ecu/drachma to trend downward in the near future and a good amount in dollars was bought after the fixing.
